newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rail robber who drugged victims is jailed.
newsitem.headline: Polish rail robber who drugged victims is jailed.

text.p: A robber, who gave drug-laced drinks to fellow train passengers before robbing them in attacks that led to the deaths of two people, was sentenced to 15 years in prison in a western Poland court on Thursday.
PAP news agency said the Poznan provincial court heard that in 1991 and 1992 the accused drugged 26 victims and two died.

The man, identified only as Antoni O., rode around the country amiably offering travel companions vodka mixed with a fizzy drink containing a powerful cocktail of drugs. He stole from them after they slumped into unconsciousness.

He was sentenced to 26 prisons terms of six to 15 years but the court was was obliged under Polish law to make them concurrent, PAP reported. It quoted Judge Pawel Spaleniak as saying there was no proof the man meant his victims to die.
The verdict is open to appeal. Under Polish law, the surnames of people involved in criminal cases are not revealed.
